page: Amazon Web Services c7a.32xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor architecture, featuring 128 dedicated physical cores powered by AMD EPYC 9R14 processors clocked at 3.7 GHz. Utilizing the x86_64 architecture with one thread per core, the system provides 256.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, maintaining a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio (2.0 GB per core). Local storage is absent, requiring external storage volumes for stateful persistence, and the platform incorporates a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps with no bundled GPU acceleration.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate exceptional multi-core and vector compute throughput. The system reaches top-tier results in stress-ng multi-core testing (392,789.86) and PassMark CPU score (128,733.18), supported by full instruction set features including AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16. Memory bandwidth is similarly prominent, achieving 565.2 GB/sec on uncached 256 MB reads and 294.16 GB/sec on writes. In application-focused metrics, the instance registers 261.89 million Redis SET operations per second and demonstrates high software compilation throughput with Clang (75,929.0).

Cost efficiency is strongly aligned with massive parallel processing tasks where high instruction throughput and memory bandwidth per vCPU can be fully leveraged. Because memory is capped at 2.0 GB per vCPU and local NVMe storage is omitted, the profile presents a tradeoff for memory-bound analytics or IOPS-heavy local data operations, which must accommodate remote storage latencies. Workloads best aligned with the c7a.32xlarge include large-scale continuous integration and compilation pipelines, high-concurrency microservices, batch processing, and CPU-based machine learning prompt processing.
description: Amazon Web Services c7a.32xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server powered by 128 dedicated cores of AMD EPYC 9R14 processors at 3.7 GHz on the x86_64 Nitro platform. Equipped with 256.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz, it maintains a 2 GB per core density without integrated GPUs or local storage disks, while providing 50 Gbps baseline networking. Benchmark evaluations reflect top-tier capabilities across multi-core computing (PassMark CPU score of 128,733.18), AVX-512 vector operations, uncached memory bandwidth reaching 565.2 GB/sec read, and high-volume caching (261.89 million Redis SET operations per second). Designed for compute-heavy parallel applications, the instance functions effectively for large-scale software compilation, CPU-driven batch simulations, high-throughput distributed microservices, and LLM prompt processing workloads.
